revision_notes: The confirmed UXP interoperability platform (launched 25 Sept 2025, implementation targeted May 2026) covers 12 pilot institutions and does not include the Ministry of Education. Côte d'Ivoire's separate education digitisation strategy (SNDECI 2024-2028) covers standalone platforms (SIGE, "Mon École à la Maison", online enrolment) with no documented link to the government data exchange, and no source names education as a near-term integration target. Comments: E-health services are mentioned in the National Digital Development Strategy. The e-Government program includes plans for e-health. Raxio data centre is operational in Côte d'Ivoire for data hosting. No specific documentation of health system integration with the UXP pilot.

revision_notes: CNAM, which administers the CMU health insurance scheme, is confirmed as one of the 12 pilot institutions in the officially launched UXP interoperability platform (25 Sept 2025), with implementation targeted for May 2026, and a July 2024 decree makes the CMU number the mandatory unique health identifier across all public and private health facilities. This is firmer evidence than "Planned" — integration is confirmed underway, so upgraded to Under development. The original we.hse.ru source was unrelated (it profiles DRC, not Côte d'Ivoire) and has been dropped.

revision_notes: Confirmed: the SDSI 2026-2030 (adopted Dec 2025, CFA10.156bn/44 projects) commits the Ministry of Economy, Planning and Development to platform interconnection, but neither the ministry nor the national statistics agency (ANStat/INS) appear among the 12 confirmed UXP pilot institutions as of the Sept 2025 launch. ANStat already draws on other agencies' administrative data (civil registration, customs, tax) for statistics production, but this predates and is independent of the UXP exchange. Evidence still supports Planned rather than Under development; score confirmed unchanged.

Definition: Whether primary laws, acts, or legal instruments exist that establish authority for cross-government data sharing and govern the data exchange system
Comments: Law No. 2013-450 on Personal Data Protection (2013) provides data protection framework enforced by ARTCI. Cybersecurity law being finalized. Référentiel Général de Sécurité des Systèmes d'Information (RGSSI) under development. No specific interoperability/data sharing law yet. The SDSI 2026-2030 identifies regulatory gaps. National Digital Economy Development Strategy includes legal framework as pillar. Substantial enabling legislation exists but interoperability-specific law is missing.
redteam_note: Comment wording may not match the score — re-read (needs judgement).
revision_notes: The original comment understated the legal basis, citing only the 2013 data protection law and asserting no interoperability-specific law exists. In fact Ordonnance n°2017-500 (2 Aug 2017) on e-services establishes an interoperability framework, and Décret n°2021-913 (22 Dec 2021) adopts a binding Référentiel Général d'Interopérabilité des Systèmes d'Information, alongside Décret n°2021-911 (data reference architecture) and Décret n°2021-917 (security audit/certification enforced by ARTCI) — all verified on ANSSI Côte d'Ivoire's official regulations page. These directly establish legal authority for cross-government data sharing, so Yes (3) is confirmed, on firmer and more relevant grounds than originally cited.
